privacy_note: All examples are synthetic composites. No names, contact details, addresses, document numbers, or raw worker narratives are included.
recording_method: Use these examples as the no-wait recording cache. Replace fixture responses with fresh runtime outputs before the final cut when a warmed Gemma 4 runtime is available; keep the same IDs so screenshots and narration remain stable.
why_gemma: Gemma 4 native function calling is visible in the tool_call_plan fields.
Gemma 4 multimodal understanding is visible in the platform image and document-intake scenes.
Small-enough local deployment is visible in the worker-mobile and NGO laptop scenes.
Harness traces become SFT and DPO data for the model-improvement scene.

examples.title: Job post with fee and document-control signals

input.text: Hiring overseas domestic workers. Applicant pays training, processing, and travel deductions from first six salaries. Passport kept by agency until deductions are complete.

cached_result.safe_summary: The post shifts recruitment costs to workers and describes identity-document control. The platform should hold publication for human review and present safer compliant-language guidance to the poster.
cached_result.video_line: A marketplace can stop risky recruitment language before it reaches workers.

training_use.dpo_chosen: harness response with GREP + RAG + tools
training_use.dpo_rejected: raw answer that treats the post as ordinary hiring copy

examples.title: Flyer image repeats a risky fee claim

input.text: Great overseas opportunity. Message the agency to reserve your placement.
input.image_description: Synthetic flyer text says workers repay placement, document processing, and transport costs after arrival. The flyer also says passports are collected for safekeeping by the agency.

cached_result.safe_summary: The visible flyer content carries the risk signal even though the caption is vague. The moderation decision should be based on both text and image evidence.
cached_result.video_line: This is why multimodal understanding is load-bearing: the risky claim is in the image, not just the caption.

training_use.sft_target: multimodal risk explanation with image-grounded findings
training_use.dpo_chosen: answer that cites image evidence and refuses unsafe optimization
training_use.dpo_rejected: text-only answer that misses the flyer

examples.title: Case bundle becomes a reviewable intake packet

documents: recruitment chat excerpt generalized to fee and travel-deduction claims
contract clause summary describing identity-document safekeeping language

extracted_factoids: recruitment costs appear shifted to the worker
identity-document control appears in contract language
wage deductions appear recurring rather than one-time
cached_result.safe_summary: The caseworker sees a timeline, legal references, questions to ask next, and a draft complaint outline. No automated report is sent; the human decides.
cached_result.video_line: The NGO gets a structured packet without uploading private case material to the public hub.

training_use.sft_target: structured intake packet with uncertainty labels
training_use.dpo_chosen: cautious draft that asks for verification and keeps the case local
training_use.dpo_rejected: overconfident legal conclusion or automatic reporting language

examples.surface: worker mobile chat and opt-in sharing
examples.title: Worker receives local guidance and can share an anonymized signal

input.worker_question: The agency says my documents will be held until deductions are paid. Is that normal?

cached_result.worker_answer: This may be a serious warning sign. Keep control of your identity documents when possible, avoid paying new fees without verified written authority, and contact a trusted local organization or official channel before replying.

share_packet_preview.summary: An anonymized corridor-level pattern indicates document-control language paired with repayment pressure.

cached_result.video_line: Sharing is opt-in and anonymized: the worker's chat stays on the phone, while the pattern can help NGOs spot a corridor trend.

training_use.sft_target: empathetic mobile answer plus opt-in explanation
training_use.dpo_rejected: answer that sends raw chat text to the hub

examples.surface: email vetting and knowledge-pack release loop
examples.title: Factoid candidates become reviewed knowledge-pack updates

input.factoid: Public-source review suggests a complaint-channel citation should be updated for the corridor pack.
input.stakeholder_request: Please verify whether this public citation is current and appropriate for worker-facing guidance.

email_loop: automation drafts a concise review request
workers and NGOs pull the updated pack
cached_result.video_line: The system closes the loop: local observations and public research become vetted updates that workers can download later.

training_use.sft_target: curator-safe review request and release note
training_use.dpo_chosen: answer that keeps humans in the approval path
training_use.dpo_rejected: answer that auto-publishes a factoid without verification

finetuning_best_practices.minimum_demo_dataset: A small synthetic/composite SFT sample plus DPO pairs is enough for the video, but a real run should use the A-00 lineage-aware train/validation split and hold out the evaluation prompts.
finetuning_best_practices.use_harness_to_generate: Yes. Treat harness outputs as silver data: record prompt, raw Gemma answer, GREP hits, RAG citations, tool calls, final harness answer, rubric grade, and provenance. Human/curator review or deterministic gates decide which rows become training examples.
do_not_train_on: names, contact details, addresses, identity numbers
